section.sectionSummaryBrief: Opening lines of the maamar with the date 19 Kislev 5726.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
19 Kislev 5726

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Alter Rebbe's redemption is connected to the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" and the dissemination of Chassidus.
section.t: "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me, for many were with me."
And our master, the Alter Rebbe, writes
(the master of redemption and joy),
"And when I read in the Book of Tehillim the verse 'He redeemed my soul in peace,'
before I began the verse after it,
I went out in peace from the One who is Peace."
And it is understood from this,
that the content of the verse is connected to the redemption of our master, the Alter Rebbe.
And behold, the redemption of our master, the Alter Rebbe, is the matter of the dissemination of the wellsprings
(of the teachings of Chassidus, even to)
the outside.
And as is known,
that the cause of the prosecution and imprisonment below was due to the debate above regarding the dissemination of the secrets of Torah in a revealed manner, until it reaches each and every one.
And when there was a verdict above to disseminate the secrets of Torah
(and on the contrary,
with greater vigor and strength than before the imprisonment)
the verdict below was automatically nullified,
and he went out to freedom.
For from this it is understood,
that the content of the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace" is connected to the matter of disseminating the teachings of Chassidus.
And behold, our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"'He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me, etc.'
The Holy One, blessed be He, said,
'Whoever engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, I consider it as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world.'"
And based on this, it can be said,
that in addition to the connection of the dissemination of the teachings of Chassidus to the content of the verse as it is in its simple sense
(for a verse does not depart from its simple meaning)
— redemption in peace,
it
(the dissemination of the teachings of Chassidus)
is also connected to the matter of one who engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The simple explanation of the verse and the division of Torah, kindness, and communal prayer into two categories.
section.t: B)
And behold, the simple explanation of this verse is,
that "for many were with me" is a reason given for "He redeemed my soul in peace."
That is, it is possible for redemption to be in a manner of war,
and the advantage of this redemption is — "He redeemed in peace."
And the reason for this, that He redeemed my soul in peace, is,
"for many were with me."
And it is necessary to understand what is the matter of specifically "He redeemed in peace,"
and the connection of "for many were with me" to "He redeemed in peace."
And behold, in the exposition of our sages, of blessed memory, on this verse,
"Whoever engages in Torah, acts of kindness, and prays with the congregation, etc.,"
Rashi explains,
"Torah, as it is written,
'and all its paths are peace,'
and likewise acts of kindness are also peace,
and praying with the congregation is the matter of 'for many were with me'"
(as Rashi explains there,
"'for many were with me' —
that they prayed with me").
And that is,
that these three matters,
Torah, acts of kindness, and prayer with the congregation,
are divided by them into two categories.
Torah and acts of kindness are the matter of "in peace,"
and prayer with the congregation is the matter of "for many were with me."
And it is necessary to understand why they divide these three matters into two categories.
Also, it is necessary to understand what they said, "Whoever engages, etc.,"
that it speaks here about the matter of the person who engages in Torah, etc., and not about the matter of Torah, acts of kindness, and prayer with the congregation themselves.
As is the common expression in many places,
like "The world stands on three things: on Torah, on service, and on acts of kindness"
(and not "whoever engages in Torah, service, and acts of kindness sustains the world"),
and the expression here is "whoever engages, etc."
